description: "On the shared /data neurico host, API keys may be absent; GPUs are shared/contended; vLLM recipe, cached models, and pitfalls (pkill self-kill, cudnn clash, prompt_logprobs OOM)"

---

Observed 2026-10-14 and 2026-10-16 in neurico research workspaces on this host:
- OPENROUTER_KEY / OPENAI keys were NOT set in the session env (`~/.flamebird/neurico/.env` has it commented out). Resource-finder stage may be skipped (no papers/, datasets/, code/).
- Local models + datasets cached in `/data/transformers/hub` (HF_HOME=/data/transformers): Qwen2.5-{0.5,1.5,3,7,14}B-Instruct safetensors, Qwen3/3.5 family, Llama-3.1-8B, GGUFs; datasets incl. glue(sst2 only), stanfordnlp/sst2, samsum, ag_news, boolq, mmlu. huggingface.co is reachable for extra downloads (curl resolve/main URLs).
- 2026-10-16: 4x RTX A6000 (48GB) present but shared — other users' jobs held ~42GB on 3 GPUs and intermittently grabbed the 4th. Approach that worked: vLLM 0.31 (`uv add "vllm>=0.10"`; unpinned `uv add vllm` resolved an ancient 0.4 build), small `gpu_memory_utilization` (~0.11 ≈ 5GB) for ≤1.5B models on the leftover slices, plus a bash wrapper that polls `nvidia-smi` free memory and retries launch. vLLM checks free mem ≥ util×total at startup.
- 2026-10-14 (no GPU then): llama.cpp multi-server CPU fallback worked; `transformers` CPU generation much slower.
- Pitfalls: `pkill -f <pattern>` inside a Bash call whose text contains the pattern kills the calling shell (find PIDs, kill by PID separately). Leftover `nvidia-cudnn-cu12` 8.x from a failed install breaks flashinfer ("Found 2 libcudnn.so.x") — `uv pip uninstall nvidia-cudnn-cu12`. vLLM `prompt_logprobs` materialises full-vocab logits → OOM on small slices; cap `max_num_batched_tokens` (~1024). Don't edit a bash script while a running loop is executing it.
- Label-restricted log-probs in vLLM: `logprobs_mode="processed_logprobs"` + `allowed_token_ids=label_ids` returns log-softmax renormalised over the labels.

Update 2026-10-16 (inter-model-agreement workspace): 4×A6000 present but shared — other neurico sessions keep each GPU at ~6–10 GB free, fluctuating second to second. What worked:
- `uv venv --python 3.12` (default 3.14 breaks vLLM); pyproject needs `requires-python="==3.12.*"` and `[tool.uv] package=false`.
- vLLM 0.31: no bitsandbytes; set `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` (JIT build fails); `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`.
- Use pre-quantized 4-bit AWQ/GPTQ checkpoints (~5.5 GB for 8B): Qwen/*-AWQ, hugging-quants Llama-3.1/gemma-2 AWQ-INT4, tiiuae/Falcon3-7B-Instruct-AWQ, solidrust Mistral AWQ, kaitchup Olmo-3/Phi-3 GPTQ.
- Cap gpu_memory_utilization to ~12.5 GB and retry on startup OOM via a scheduler loop; max_model_len 2560, max_num_seqs 64.
- Gated models in /data/transformers/hub (meta-llama Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, google/gemma-7b-it) have weights but no config/tokenizer → unusable; unsloth mirror of Llama-3.1 is complete. Disk /data is ~100% full.

Update 2026-10-16 (few-shot-ordering workspace, 2nd session): a "Begin research execution" prompt can land on a workspace where a prior session already finished most work (REPORT.md exists, background jobs killed at session end). Check logs/*.status and REPORT first and resume only the interrupted pieces rather than restarting. Monitor `tail -n0 -F` on status files missed an append; poll status files directly instead. - GPUs 0/1 top out at exactly 5125 MiB free (other users' 43 GB jobs) → budget ≤4.4 GB per slice. Multi-GPU TP rarely gets simultaneous slices; a queue with alternative configs ("1:9.5,2:4.4") was what worked. TP shards must keep quant groups aligned (Qwen2.5-3B intermediate 11008/4 not divisible by 128).
- HF `device_map` sharding needs `accelerate` installed (not pulled in by vllm).
- Self-kill again: `pkill -f`/`grep '[x]pat'` still matches if the SAME command line also contains the pattern elsewhere (e.g. a later nohup). Kill by PID in a separate call.
- Contended-GPU timings: 7–8B bf16 on a 20 GB slice ~2–8 min/level for 1.6k prompts once GPU2 freed (~17:00–19:00); Phi-3 (KV-heavy) on 13 GB of a 100%-util GPU took 33 min.

New vLLM startup failure on contended GPUs: "Error in memory profiling … other processes release GPU memory" — just retry. HotpotQA distractor prompts reach ~2.4k tokens; use max_model_len ≥4096.

- GPUs saturated again from ~13:00 (other neurico sessions + liuxiao TP job); GPU0/1 "5125 MiB free" is another job's fluctuating activation memory — launches there fail even when the check passes. A single scheduler (one launch per GPU per 120 s) beats per-job wait loops, which raced each other (4 OOMs at once when GPU2 briefly freed 29 GB).

Update 2026-10-21 (cot_verbosity_tax workspace, 6+ concurrent neurico sessions): GPUs were ~fully oversubscribed; launches failed ~80% from free-memory races. Lessons:
- Long multi-round generation (budget forcing, 12 rounds × up to 2k tokens) on a 100%-util shared GPU is very slow: 7B-AWQ forced arm took ~4 h incl. a ~60 min final answer pass (small KV → ~15 concurrent long contexts). Budget for it, or cut rounds/items for ≥7B.
- My own jobs on the same GPU slow each other badly — don't stack 7B+14B+alt runs on one GPU.

"""Greedy generation for every prompt in data/prompts.jsonl with one model (vLLM).

Usage: python src/generate.py --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --name qwen0.5b --gpu-gb 4.5

Outputs append to results/gen/<name>.jsonl (resumable: finished uids are skipped).
The chat template's default system prompt is kept, as a deployed model would use it.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import time

os.environ.setdefault("HF_HOME", "/data/transformers")
os.environ.setdefault("HF_HUB_OFFLINE", "1")
os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER", "0")
# In-process engine (faster startup); TP workers are forked from this process so they inherit
# the memory-snapshot patch below.
os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING", "0")
os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD", "fork")

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
CHUNK = 3000


def gpu_total_gb():
    dev = os.environ.get("CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES", "0").split(",")[0]
    out = subprocess.check_output(["nvidia-smi", "-i", dev, "--query-gpu=memory.total",
                                   "--format=csv,noheader,nounits"]).decode()
    return float(out.strip()) / 1024


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--model", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--name", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--gpu-gb", type=float, default=4.5)
    ap.add_argument("--max-model-len", type=int, default=2560)
    ap.add_argument("--max-num-seqs", type=int, default=48)
    ap.add_argument("--batched-tokens", type=int, default=1024)
    ap.add_argument("--tp", type=int, default=1, help="tensor parallel size")
    ap.add_argument("--exps", default="cls,ifev,ext")
    ap.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=0, help="smoke test: items per (exp,task)")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

    exps = set(args.exps.split(","))
    prompts = [json.loads(l) for l in open(os.path.join(ROOT, "data", "prompts.jsonl"))]
    prompts = [p for p in prompts if p["exp"] in exps]
    if args.limit:
        ifev_keys = sorted({p["item"] for p in prompts if p["exp"] == "ifev"})[:args.limit]
        prompts = [p for p in prompts if (p["item"] in ifev_keys if p["exp"] == "ifev" else p["item"] < args.limit)]
    out_dir = os.path.join(ROOT, "results", "gen")
    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
    out_path = os.path.join(out_dir, f"{args.name}{'_smoke' if args.limit else ''}.jsonl")
    done = set()
    if os.path.exists(out_path):
        done = {json.loads(l)["uid"] for l in open(out_path)}
    todo = [p for p in prompts if p["uid"] not in done]
    print(f"[{args.name}] {len(todo)} to do ({len(done)} done)", flush=True)
    if not todo:
        return

    if args.tp > 1:
        # Each TP worker creates its CUDA context + NCCL buffers (~0.8 GB) *before* vLLM measures
        # free memory, so the vLLM budget must be ~0.4 GB below the slice the queue reserved.
        args.gpu_gb -= 0.4
    util = min(0.95, args.gpu_gb / gpu_total_gb())
    if args.tp == 1:
        # Shared-GPU race fix: grab the memory in *this* process as soon as it is free, and
        # release it inside vLLM's worker right before it measures free memory (in-process
        # engine), so other jobs cannot take it during vLLM's slow startup.
        import torch
        import vllm.v1.worker.gpu_worker as gw
        hold, deadline = [], time.time() + 180
        while not hold and time.time() < deadline:
            try:
                hold.append(torch.empty(int((args.gpu_gb + 0.3) * 1024 ** 3), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda"))
            except torch.OutOfMemoryError:
                time.sleep(0.3)
        if not hold:
            print("HOLD_TIMEOUT: could not reserve GPU memory", flush=True)
            return 3
        _snapshot = gw.MemorySnapshot

        def _release_then_snapshot(*a, **k):
            if hold:
                hold.clear()
                torch.cuda.empty_cache()
            return _snapshot(*a, **k)
        gw.MemorySnapshot = _release_then_snapshot
    else:
        # Tensor parallel: one holder process per GPU reserves the memory; each forked worker kills
        # the holder of its own GPU right before vLLM measures free memory.
        import signal
        import vllm.v1.worker.gpu_worker as gw
        phys = os.environ["CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"].split(",")
        holders = {}
        for i, g in enumerate(phys):
            holders[i] = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, os.path.join(ROOT, "src", "hold_gpu.py"),
                                           str(args.gpu_gb - 0.5), "180"], stdout=subprocess.PIPE, text=True,
                                          env=dict(os.environ, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=g))
        if any(h.stdout.readline().strip() != "READY" for h in holders.values()):
            for h in holders.values():
                h.kill()
            print("HOLD_TIMEOUT: could not reserve GPU memory", flush=True)
            return 3
        _snapshot = gw.MemorySnapshot

        def _release_then_snapshot(*a, **k):
            import torch
            h = holders.pop(torch.cuda.current_device(), None)
            if h is not None:
                os.kill(h.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
                t0 = time.time()
                while torch.cuda.mem_get_info()[0] < args.gpu_gb * 1024 ** 3 and time.time() - t0 < 10:
                    time.sleep(0.02)
                torch.cuda.empty_cache()

# Planning: System Prompt Saturation

## Motivation & Novelty Assessment

### Why This Research Matters
Production system prompts routinely run to thousands of tokens and dozens of rules (personas, formatting,
safety, tool policies). Practitioners assume every rule added is a rule followed. If per-rule compliance decays with
length, rule count, rule position, or rule conflicts, prompt authors need quantitative guidance on how many rules a
model of a given size can carry and where to put the important ones.

### Gap in Existing Work
The resource-finder stage produced no `literature_review.md`, `papers/`, `datasets/` or `code/` in this workspace
(and no API keys are configured), so the review below is from background knowledge. Related work:
IFEval (Zhou et al., 2023) measures compliance with 1–3 verifiable instructions in the *user* turn; "Lost in the
Middle" (Liu et al., 2023) shows U-shaped position effects for *retrieval*; ManyIFEval / "Curse of instructions"
(Harada et al., 2024/25) shows that the probability of following *all* instructions falls with their count;
FollowBench / ComplexBench add constraints incrementally. What is missing is a single controlled study that, in the
**system prompt**, separates (a) total length (holding rule count fixed), (b) rule count, (c) rule position, and
(d) contradictory rules, and does so across a size ladder of open models with *per-rule* (not all-or-nothing) metrics.

### Our Novel Contribution
A factorial, programmatically-scored benchmark of 40 mutually compatible verifiable system-prompt rules plus
4 conflict pairs, run on 9 open instruction models from 0.5B to 14B, with paired designs (same user queries across
conditions) and baseline (no-rule) rates to correct for rules that are satisfied by chance.

### Experiment Justification
- **Exp A (rule count N ∈ {0,1,2,5,10,15,20,30,40})**: tests the saturation claim (sub-3B saturate at ~10 rules,
  7B+ sustain ~20). N=0 gives base rates for every rule.
- **Exp B (length, N=5 fixed, neutral filler to 0/500/1k/2k/4k/8k tokens)**: isolates length from rule count to test
  "2–5% per doubling beyond 500 tokens".
- **Position analysis (Exp A N≥10 and Exp B)**: rules are randomly ordered/inserted, so relative position is
  randomized; tests "first/last 20% followed 15–25% more often than middle".
- **Exp D (conflicts)**: X-only vs Y-only vs X+Y for 4 contradictory pairs, holding rule count fixed; tests
  "conflict drops compliance on both by 20–30%".

## Research Question
How does per-rule compliance with system-prompt rules depend on prompt length, rule count, rule position and
rule conflicts, and does the saturation point scale with model size?

## Hypothesis Decomposition
- H1: per-rule compliance falls 2–5 pp (relative) per doubling of system prompt length beyond 500 tokens (fixed N).
- H2: rules in the first and last 20% of the prompt are followed 15–25% (relative) more often than middle rules.
- H3: adding a contradicting rule lowers compliance on each member of the pair by 20–30% (relative).
- H4: per-rule compliance in models <3B degrades past ~10 rules; ≥7B models hold up to ~20 rules.

## Proposed Methodology
- Models (local, vLLM, greedy, temperature 0): Qwen2.5-Instruct 0.5B/1.5B/3B/7B/14B(AWQ), Llama-3.2-Instruct 1B/3B,
  Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen3-8B (non-thinking). Real models; no simulation. No API key available.
- User queries: 100 open-ended instructions from Alpaca-cleaned (no input field), same 100 in every cell (paired).
- Rules: 40 verifiable rules (keyword inclusion, start/end phrases, formatting, exclusion, punctuation).
  Each scored by a deterministic Python checker. Random subset and order per item (seeded).
- Filler: Wikipedia (WikiText-103) paragraphs presented as reference material; rules inserted as standalone
  "Response rule:" paragraphs at random paragraph boundaries.
- Metrics: per-rule compliance (mean of binary checks), baseline-corrected lift over N=0, all-rules-followed rate.
- Statistics: item-clustered bootstrap 95% CIs; mixed/fixed-effect logistic regressions with rule fixed effects
  (log2 length slope; position bins; conflict indicator); McNemar-style paired tests for conflict; Holm correction
  across the hypothesis families. α = 0.05.

## Expected Outcomes
Support for H1: negative log2-length slope of 2–5% relative beyond 500 tokens. H2: U-shape with edge/middle ratio
1.15–1.25. H3: conflict ratio 0.70–0.80. H4: knee at ~10 rules for small, ~20 for large models.
Any other pattern (no slope, monotone position effect, a model winning one side of a conflict) refutes/qualifies.

## Timeline
Setup+prompt build 45 min; generation 2–4 h (shared GPUs); scoring/analysis 1 h; report 45 min.

## Potential Challenges
Shared GPUs (one 48 GB GPU reserved with a holder; small models on ~5 GB slices); checkers may be too strict/lenient
(audit samples); filler content could confound (use neutral encyclopedic text, randomized per item).

## Success Criteria
All four hypotheses tested with CIs on ≥6 models; report states clearly which are supported.

import json
import os
import random
import re

import pandas as pd
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

from rules import BANK, CONFLICTS, CONFLICT_BASE_POOL

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
HUB = "/data/transformers/hub"
N_ITEMS = 100
SEED = 42
COUNTS = [0, 1, 2, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 40]
FILLER_TOKENS = [0, 500, 1000, 2000, 4000, 8000]

PREAMBLE = "You are a helpful assistant."
LIST_HEADER = "Follow these rules in every response:"
B_HEADER = ("You are a helpful assistant. The reference material below is provided for background only. "
            "Rules for your responses are marked \"Response rule:\" and appear throughout this prompt; follow all of them.")


def load_queries(rng):
    snap = os.path.join(HUB, "datasets--yahma--alpaca-cleaned", "snapshots")
    path = os.path.join(snap, os.listdir(snap)[0], "alpaca_data_cleaned.json")
    data = json.load(open(path))
    ok = re.compile(r"^(Explain|Describe|Write|What|How|Why|Give|Tell|Discuss|Summarize|Suggest|Compare|Create|Generate)\b")
    bad = re.compile(r"(sentence|word|rewrite|translate|code|program|function|poem|haiku|list of \d|\d+ words|tweet|"
                     r"classify|title|headline|slogan|edit|grammar|haiku|limerick|acronym|synonym|antonym)", re.I)
    cands = [d["instruction"].strip() for d in data
             if not d["input"].strip() and ok.match(d["instruction"]) and not bad.search(d["instruction"])
             and 30 <= len(d["instruction"]) <= 160 and len(d["output"].split()) >= 80]
    cands = sorted(set(cands))
    return rng.sample(cands, N_ITEMS)


def load_filler_paragraphs():
    snap = os.path.join(HUB, "datasets--Salesforce--wikitext", "snapshots")
    path = os.path.join(snap, os.listdir(snap)[0], "wikitext-103-raw-v1", "validation-00000-of-00001.parquet")
    lines = pd.read_parquet(path)["text"].tolist()

    for l in lines:

            for kind, v in blocks:
                if kind == "rule":

            rows.append(dict(exp="B", cond=f"L{L}", n_rules=5, filler_budget=L, item=i, rules=ids, pos=pos, system=sysp))

        for i in range(N_ITEMS):
            base = rng.sample(CONFLICT_BASE_POOL, 5)  # 4 background + 1 neutral stand-in

                    ids_txt.append((x[0], x[1]))
                if cond in ("Y", "XY"):
                    ids_txt.append((y[0], y[1]))
                if cond != "XY":
                    ids_txt.append((base[4], text[base[4]]))
                r2 = random.Random(f"{pair}-{i}")  # same order skeleton across the 3 conditions
                r2.shuffle(ids_txt)

                pos = [j / (len(ids) - 1) for j in range(len(ids))]
                rows.append(dict(exp="D", cond=f"{pair}:{cond}", pair=pair, item=i, rules=ids, pos=pos, system=sysp))

        r["uid"] = f"{r['exp']}|{r['cond']}|{r['item']}"
        r["query"] = queries[r["item"]]
        r["sys_tokens_qwen"] = len(tok.encode(r["system"]))

            f.write(json.dumps(r, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

        json.dump(queries, f, indent=1)
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    print(df.groupby(["exp", "cond"]).sys_tokens_qwen.agg(["count", "mean", "min", "max"]).to_string())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Greedy generation for every prompt in data/prompts.jsonl with one model (vLLM, in-process engine).

Usage: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2 python src/generate.py --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct --name qwen2.5-7b --gpu-gb 20 \
           [--holder-ctl logs/hold_gpu2.target --holder-gb 40]

Outputs append to results/gen/<name>.jsonl (resumable: finished uids are skipped).
Shared-GPU race fix: memory is grabbed with a placeholder tensor as soon as it is free (optionally after shrinking
my own holder process), and released inside vLLM right before it measures free memory.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import time

os.environ.setdefault("HF_HOME", "/data/transformers")
os.environ.setdefault("HF_HUB_OFFLINE", "1")
os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER", "0")
os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING", "0")

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
CHUNK = 900
MAX_TOKENS = 700


def gpu_total_gb():
    dev = os.environ.get("CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES", "0").split(",")[0]
    out = subprocess.check_output(["nvidia-smi", "-i", dev, "--query-gpu=memory.total",
                                   "--format=csv,noheader,nounits"]).decode()
    return float(out.strip()) / 1024


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--model", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--name", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--gpu-gb", type=float, default=4.5)
    ap.add_argument("--max-model-len", type=int, default=10240)
    ap.add_argument("--max-num-seqs", type=int, default=64)
    ap.add_argument("--batched-tokens", type=int, default=4096)
    ap.add_argument("--exps", default="A,B,D")
    ap.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=0, help="smoke test: items per cell")
    ap.add_argument("--holder-ctl", default="", help="control file of my holder on this GPU")
    ap.add_argument("--holder-gb", type=int, default=40, help="holder size to restore when done")
    ap.add_argument("--eager", type=int, default=1)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    exps = set(args.exps.split(","))
    prompts = [json.loads(l) for l in open(os.path.join(ROOT, "data", "prompts.jsonl"))]
    prompts = [p for p in prompts if p["exp"] in exps and (not args.limit or p["item"] < args.limit)]
    out_dir = os.path.join(ROOT, "results", "gen")
    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
    out_path = os.path.join(out_dir, f"{args.name}{'_smoke' if args.limit else ''}.jsonl")
    done = set()
    if os.path.exists(out_path):
        done = {json.loads(l)["uid"] for l in open(out_path)}
    todo = [p for p in prompts if p["uid"] not in done]
    print(f"[{args.name}] {len(todo)} to do ({len(done)} done)", flush=True)
    if not todo:
        return 0

    import torch
    import vllm.v1.worker.gpu_worker as gw
    try:
        import vllm.utils.mem_utils as mu
    except ImportError:
        mu = None
    from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

    util = min(0.95, args.gpu_gb / gpu_total_gb())
    if args.holder_ctl:
        held = int(open(args.holder_ctl).read().strip())
        need = int(args.gpu_gb + 1.5) + 1
        open(args.holder_ctl, "w").write(str(max(0, held - need)))
    hold, deadline = [], time.time() + 600
    while not hold and time.time() < deadline:
        try:
            hold.append(torch.empty(int((args.gpu_gb + 0.3) * 1024 ** 3), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda"))
        except torch.OutOfMemoryError:
            time.sleep(0.2)
    if not hold:
        print("HOLD_TIMEOUT: could not reserve GPU memory", flush=True)
        return 75
    _snapshot = gw.MemorySnapshot

    class _ReleaseThenSnapshot(_snapshot):
        def __init__(self, *a, **k):
            if hold:
                hold.clear()
                torch.cuda.empty_cache()
            super().__init__(*a, **k)
    gw.MemorySnapshot = _ReleaseThenSnapshot
    if mu is not None and hasattr(mu, "MemorySnapshot"):
        mu.MemorySnapshot = _ReleaseThenSnapshot

    llm = LLM(model=args.model, gpu_memory_utilization=util, max_model_len=args.max_model_len,
              max_num_seqs=args.max_num_seqs, max_num_batched_tokens=args.batched_tokens,
              enforce_eager=bool(args.eager), enable_prefix_caching=True, seed=42, trust_remote_code=False)
    tok = llm.get_tokenizer()
    is_qwen3 = "qwen3" in args.model.lower()

    t0 = time.time()
    with open(out_path, "a") as fout:
        for s in range(0, len(todo), CHUNK):
            batch = todo[s:s + CHUNK]
            convs = [[{"role": "system", "content": p["system"]}, {"role": "user", "content": p["query"]}] for p in batch]
            sp = SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=MAX_TOKENS, seed=42)
            kw = dict(chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": False}) if is_qwen3 else {}
            outs = llm.chat(convs, sp, use_tqdm=False, **kw)
            for p, o in zip(batch, outs):
                c = o.outputs[0]
                fout.write(json.dumps(dict(uid=p["uid"], text=c.text, n_tokens=len(c.token_ids),
                                           n_prompt_tokens=len(o.prompt_token_ids), finish=c.finish_reason),
                                      ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
            fout.flush()
            print(f"[{args.name}] {s + len(batch)}/{len(todo)} done, {time.time() - t0:.0f}s", flush=True)
    with open(os.path.join(out_dir, f"{args.name}_template_example.txt"), "w") as f:
        f.write(tok.apply_chat_template([{"role": "system", "content": todo[0]["system"]},
                                         {"role": "user", "content": todo[0]["query"]}],
                                        tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True,
                                        **({"enable_thinking": False} if is_qwen3 else {})))
    print(f"[{args.name}] FINISHED in {time.time() - t0:.0f}s", flush=True)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    code = main()
    sys.stdout.flush()
    os._exit(code or 0)

#!/bin/bash
# Run generation jobs sequentially on one GPU, retrying while memory is unavailable.
# Usage: src/run_gpu_queue.sh <gpu> <jobfile> [holder_ctl]
# jobfile lines: <model> <name> <gpu_gb> [extra args...]
GPU=$1; JOBS=$2; CTL=$3
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
source .venv/bin/activate
while read -r MODEL NAME GB EXTRA; do
  [ -z "$MODEL" ] && continue
  for try in $(seq 1 200); do
    echo "$(date +%T) start $NAME on GPU$GPU try $try"
    if [ -n "$CTL" ]; then H="--holder-ctl $CTL"; else H=""; fi
    CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=$GPU python src/generate.py --model $MODEL --name $NAME --gpu-gb $GB $H $EXTRA >> logs/gen_$NAME.log 2>&1
    rc=$?
    [ -n "$CTL" ] && echo 40 > $CTL
    echo "$(date +%T) $NAME exit $rc"
    if [ $rc -eq 0 ] && grep -q "FINISHED\|0 to do" logs/gen_$NAME.log; then break; fi

"""Score every generation: one row per (model, prompt, rule) -> results/rule_scores.parquet.

Also scores every bank rule on the no-rule (Exp A, N=0) responses to get per-model chance/base rates
-> results/base_rates.csv.
"""
import glob
import json
import os

import pandas as pd

from rules import ALL_CHECKERS, BANK, CONFLICTS

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
CONFLICT_OF = {}
for pair, (x, y) in CONFLICTS.items():
    CONFLICT_OF[x[0]] = (pair, "X")
    CONFLICT_OF[y[0]] = (pair, "Y")


def main():
    prompts = {json.loads(l)["uid"]: json.loads(l) for l in open(os.path.join(ROOT, "data", "prompts.jsonl"))}
    rows, base, gens = [], [], []
    for path in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(ROOT, "results", "gen", "*.jsonl"))):
        model = os.path.basename(path)[:-6]
        if model.endswith("_smoke"):
            continue
        for l in open(path):
            g = json.loads(l)
            p = prompts[g["uid"]]
            t = g["text"]
            words = len(t.split())
            gens.append(dict(model=model, uid=g["uid"], exp=p["exp"], cond=p["cond"], item=p["item"],
                             n_rules=len(p["rules"]), sys_tokens=g["n_prompt_tokens"], out_tokens=g["n_tokens"],
                             finish=g["finish"], words=words))
            for j, (r, pos) in enumerate(zip(p["rules"], p["pos"])):
                pair, role = CONFLICT_OF.get(r, (None, None))
                rows.append(dict(model=model, uid=g["uid"], exp=p["exp"], cond=p["cond"], item=p["item"],
                                 n_rules=len(p["rules"]), filler=p.get("filler_budget", 0), rule=r, rank=j, pos=pos,
                                 pair=p.get("pair"), conflict_role=role, followed=int(ALL_CHECKERS[r](t)),
                                 truncated=int(g["finish"] == "length"), prompt_tokens=g["n_prompt_tokens"]))
            if p["exp"] == "A" and p["cond"] == "N0":
                for r in ALL_CHECKERS:
                    base.append(dict(model=model, item=p["item"], rule=r, followed=int(ALL_CHECKERS[r](t))))
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    df.to_parquet(os.path.join(ROOT, "results", "rule_scores.parquet"))
    pd.DataFrame(gens).to_parquet(os.path.join(ROOT, "results", "generations_meta.parquet"))
    b = pd.DataFrame(base).groupby(["model", "rule"]).followed.mean().unstack(0)
    b.to_csv(os.path.join(ROOT, "results", "base_rates.csv"))
    print(df.groupby(["model", "exp"]).followed.agg(["count", "mean"]).unstack(1).round(3).to_string())
    print("\nbase rates (N=0), mean over bank rules:")
    print(b.loc[[r[0] for r in BANK]].mean().round(3).to_string())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Statistical analysis + figures for all hypotheses. Reads results/rule_scores.parquet (from score.py).

Outputs: results/tables/*.csv, results/stats.json, figures/*.png
Uncertainty: item-clustered bootstrap (resample the 100 user queries; 2000 resamples, seed 0) unless noted.
"""
import json
import os
import warnings

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests
from scipy import stats

from rules import BANK, CONFLICTS

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
TAB = os.path.join(ROOT, "results", "tables")
FIG = os.path.join(ROOT, "figures")
os.makedirs(TAB, exist_ok=True)
os.makedirs(FIG, exist_ok=True)
B_RESAMPLES = 2000
RNG = np.random.default_rng(0)

# Model metadata: display order, parameter count (B), family
MODELS = {
    "qwen2.5-0.5b": (0.5, "Qwen2.5"), "llama3.2-1b": (1.2, "Llama-3"), "qwen2.5-1.5b": (1.5, "Qwen2.5"),
    "qwen2.5-3b": (3.1, "Qwen2.5"), "llama3.2-3b": (3.2, "Llama-3"), "qwen2.5-7b": (7.6, "Qwen2.5"),
    "llama3.1-8b": (8.0, "Llama-3"), "qwen3-8b": (8.2, "Qwen3"), "qwen2.5-14b": (14.7, "Qwen2.5"),
}
BANK_IDS = [r[0] for r in BANK]


def size_class(m):
    p = MODELS[m][0]
    return "<3B" if p < 3 else ("3B" if p < 7 else ">=7B")


def boot_items(df, stat, n=B_RESAMPLES):
    """Item-clustered bootstrap of stat(df) -> (point, lo, hi). stat takes a dataframe."""
    items = df["item"].unique()
    groups = {i: g for i, g in df.groupby("item")}
    point = stat(df)
    vals = []
    for _ in range(n):
        samp = RNG.choice(items, len(items), replace=True)
        d = pd.concat([groups[i] for i in samp], ignore_index=True)
        vals.append(stat(d))
    vals = np.array(vals)
    return point, np.nanpercentile(vals, 2.5), np.nanpercentile(vals, 97.5), vals


def item_boot_means(per_item, n=B_RESAMPLES):
    """Fast bootstrap for statistics that are means over items: per_item is an (items x k) array of per-item
    means; returns bootstrap distribution of column means (n x k)."""
    idx = RNG.integers(0, per_item.shape[0], size=(n, per_item.shape[0]))
    return np.nanmean(per_item[idx], axis=1)


def main():
    df = pd.read_parquet(os.path.join(ROOT, "results", "rule_scores.parquet"))
    df = df[df.model.isin(MODELS)]
    models = [m for m in MODELS if m in df.model.unique()]
    base = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(ROOT, "results", "base_rates.csv"), index_col=0)
    df["base"] = [base.at[r, m] if (r in base.index and m in base.columns) else np.nan for r, m in zip(df.rule, df.model)]
    out = {"models": models}

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ Exp A: rule count
    A = df[df.exp == "A"]
    rowsA = []
    for m in models:
        d = A[A.model == m]
        for n, g in d.groupby("n_rules"):
            per_item = g.groupby("item").followed.mean()
            bm = item_boot_means(per_item.values[:, None])[:, 0]
            allf = g.groupby("item").followed.min()
            lift = (g.followed - g.base).groupby(g.item).mean()
            rowsA.append(dict(model=m, n_rules=n, compliance=per_item.mean(), lo=np.percentile(bm, 2.5),
                              hi=np.percentile(bm, 97.5), all_followed=allf.mean(), base=g.base.mean(),
                              lift=lift.mean(), sys_tokens=g.prompt_tokens.mean()))
    TA = pd.DataFrame(rowsA)
    TA.to_csv(os.path.join(TAB, "expA_count.csv"), index=False)

    # Saturation point: largest N whose compliance is within 5 pp of the model's N<=2 level, and a hinge fit.
    sat = []
    for m in models:
        t = TA[TA.model == m].set_index("n_rules")
        ref = t.loc[[1, 2], "compliance"].mean()
        d = A[(A.model == m)].copy()
        # hinge regression: compliance ~ a + b1*N + b2*max(0, N-k); pick k minimizing SSE (linear prob. model)
        best = None
        for k in [2, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30]:
            d["h"] = np.maximum(0, d.n_rules - k)
            f = smf.ols("followed ~ n_rules + h + C(rule)", data=d).fit()
            if best is None or f.ssr < best[1]:
                best = (k, f.ssr, f)
        k, _, f = best
        first_drop = next((n for n in [5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 40] if t.loc[n, "compliance"] < ref - 0.05), None)
        sat.append(dict(model=m, params_b=MODELS[m][0], size_class=size_class(m), ref_N1_2=ref,
                        comp_N10=t.loc[10, "compliance"], comp_N20=t.loc[20, "compliance"],
                        comp_N40=t.loc[40, "compliance"], first_N_5pp_below_ref=first_drop,
                        hinge_k=k, slope_before=f.params["n_rules"], slope_after=f.params["n_rules"] + f.params["h"]))
    TS = pd.DataFrame(sat)
    TS.to_csv(os.path.join(TAB, "expA_saturation.csv"), index=False)
    out["saturation"] = TS.to_dict("records")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ Exp B: length at fixed N=5
    B = df[df.exp == "B"]
    rowsB, slopes = [], []
    for m in models:
        d = B[B.model == m]
        for L, g in d.groupby("filler"):
            per_item = g.groupby("item").followed.mean()
            bm = item_boot_means(per_item.values[:, None])[:, 0]
            rowsB.append(dict(model=m, filler=L, sys_tokens=g.prompt_tokens.mean(), compliance=per_item.mean(),
                              lo=np.percentile(bm, 2.5), hi=np.percentile(bm, 97.5),
                              truncated=g.truncated.mean()))
        # per-doubling slope beyond ~500 tokens: OLS on log2(prompt tokens) with rule fixed effects,
        # item-cluster-robust SEs. Relative slope = slope / mean compliance at the ~500-token condition.
        for label, sub in [("all", d), ("ge500", d[d.filler >= 500])]:
            sub = sub.assign(l2=np.log2(sub.prompt_tokens))
            f = smf.ols("followed ~ l2 + C(rule)", data=sub).fit(cov_type="cluster", cov_kwds={"groups": sub.item})
            ref = d[d.filler == 500].followed.mean()
            lg = smf.logit("followed ~ l2 + C(rule)", data=sub).fit(disp=0, cov_type="cluster",
                                                                     cov_kwds={"groups": sub.item}) \
                if sub.followed.nunique() > 1 else None
            slopes.append(dict(model=m, range=label, slope_pp_per_doubling=100 * f.params["l2"],
                               ci_lo=100 * f.conf_int().loc["l2", 0], ci_hi=100 * f.conf_int().loc["l2", 1],
                               p=f.pvalues["l2"], rel_pct_per_doubling=100 * f.params["l2"] / ref,
                               logit_or_per_doubling=float(np.exp(lg.params["l2"])) if lg is not None else np.nan,
                               comp_500=ref, comp_8000=d[d.filler == 8000].followed.mean()))
    TB = pd.DataFrame(rowsB)
    TB.to_csv(os.path.join(TAB, "expB_length.csv"), index=False)
    TBs = pd.DataFrame(slopes)
    TBs["p_holm"] = np.nan
    msk = TBs.range == "ge500"
    TBs.loc[msk, "p_holm"] = multipletests(TBs.loc[msk, "p"], method="holm")[1]
    TBs.to_csv(os.path.join(TAB, "expB_slopes.csv"), index=False)
    # pooled across models (model x rule fixed effects)
    sub = B[B.filler >= 500].assign(l2=lambda x: np.log2(x.prompt_tokens))
    f = smf.ols("followed ~ l2 + C(rule):C(model) + C(model)", data=sub).fit(
        cov_type="cluster", cov_kwds={"groups": sub.item})
    out["expB_pooled_ge500"] = dict(slope_pp=100 * f.params["l2"], lo=100 * f.conf_int().loc["l2", 0],
                                    hi=100 * f.conf_int().loc["l2", 1], p=f.pvalues["l2"],
                                    rel_pct=100 * f.params["l2"] / B[B.filler == 500].followed.mean())

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ Position (A N>=10, B L>=1000, E)
    P = df[((df.exp == "A") & (df.n_rules >= 10)) | ((df.exp == "B") & (df.filler >= 1000)) | (df.exp == "E")].copy()
    P["bin"] = pd.cut(P.pos, [-0.01, 0.2, 0.8, 1.01], labels=["first20", "middle", "last20"])
    P["dec"] = np.minimum((P.pos * 10).astype(int), 9)
    P["src"] = P.exp.map({"A": "list (Exp A)", "B": "interleaved, N=5 (Exp B)", "E": "interleaved, 4k tok (Exp E)"})
    rowsP = []
    for m in models + ["ALL"]:
        for src in ["ALL"] + sorted(P.src.unique()):
            d = P if m == "ALL" else P[P.model == m]
            d = d if src == "ALL" else d[d.src == src]
            if d.empty:
                continue
            # per-item means by bin -> bootstrap ratio of edges to middle
            pi = d.pivot_table(index="item", columns="bin", values="followed", aggfunc="mean", observed=False)
            pi = pi[["first20", "middle", "last20"]].values
            bm = item_boot_means(pi)
            edge = lambda a: (a[..., 0] + a[..., 2]) / 2
            ratio_b = edge(bm) / bm[:, 1]
            pt = np.nanmean(pi, axis=0)
            # regression with rule (and condition) fixed effects, cluster by item
            f = smf.ols("followed ~ C(bin, Treatment('middle')) + C(rule) + C(cond)" +
                        (" + C(model)" if m == "ALL" else ""), data=d).fit(
                cov_type="cluster", cov_kwds={"groups": d.item})
            rowsP.append(dict(model=m, source=src, n=len(d), first20=pt[0], middle=pt[1], last20=pt[2],
                              edge_mid_ratio=edge(pt) / pt[1], ratio_lo=np.nanpercentile(ratio_b, 2.5),
                              ratio_hi=np.nanpercentile(ratio_b, 97.5),
                              fe_first_pp=100 * f.params["C(bin, Treatment('middle'))[T.first20]"],
                              fe_first_p=f.pvalues["C(bin, Treatment('middle'))[T.first20]"],
                              fe_last_pp=100 * f.params["C(bin, Treatment('middle'))[T.last20]"],
                              fe_last_p=f.pvalues["C(bin, Treatment('middle'))[T.last20]"]))
    TP = pd.DataFrame(rowsP)
    TP.to_csv(os.path.join(TAB, "position.csv"), index=False)
    dec = P.groupby(["src", "dec"]).followed.mean().unstack(0)
    dec.to_csv(os.path.join(TAB, "position_deciles.csv"))
    decm = P.groupby(["model", "dec"]).followed.mean().unstack(0)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ Exp D: conflicts
    D = df[df.exp == "D"].copy()
    D["c"] = D.cond.str.split(":").str[1]
    rowsD = []
    for m in models + ["ALL"]:
        for pair, (x, y) in CONFLICTS.items():
            for role, rid, alone in [("X", x[0], "X"), ("Y", y[0], "Y")]:
                d = D[(D.pair == pair) & (D.rule == rid)]
                d = d if m == "ALL" else d[d.model == m]
                a = d[d.c == alone].set_index(["model", "item"]).followed
                b = d[d.c == "XY"].set_index(["model", "item"]).followed
                j = pd.concat([a.rename("alone"), b.rename("both")], axis=1).dropna()
                n01 = int(((j.alone == 1) & (j.both == 0)).sum())
                n10 = int(((j.alone == 0) & (j.both == 1)).sum())
                p = stats.binomtest(n01, n01 + n10).pvalue if n01 + n10 else 1.0
                per_item = j.groupby(level="item").mean().values
                bm = item_boot_means(per_item)
                rel_b = (bm[:, 1] - bm[:, 0]) / bm[:, 0]
                rowsD.append(dict(model=m, pair=pair, role=role, rule=rid, alone=j.alone.mean(), both=j.both.mean(),
                                  diff_pp=100 * (j.both.mean() - j.alone.mean()),
                                  rel_change=(j.both.mean() - j.alone.mean()) / j.alone.mean() if j.alone.mean() else np.nan,
                                  rel_lo=np.nanpercentile(rel_b, 2.5), rel_hi=np.nanpercentile(rel_b, 97.5),
                                  mcnemar_p=p, n=len(j)))
    TD = pd.DataFrame(rowsD)
    msk = TD.model != "ALL"
    TD.loc[msk, "p_holm"] = multipletests(TD.loc[msk, "mcnemar_p"], method="holm")[1]
    TD.to_csv(os.path.join(TAB, "expD_conflict.csv"), index=False)
    # both members followed? and "who wins" in XY
    win = []
    for m in models:
        for pair, (x, y) in CONFLICTS.items():
            d = D[(D.model == m) & (D.pair == pair) & (D.c == "XY")]
            w = d.pivot_table(index="item", columns="rule", values="followed")
            win.append(dict(model=m, pair=pair, X_only=((w[x[0]] == 1) & (w[y[0]] == 0)).mean(),
                            Y_only=((w[x[0]] == 0) & (w[y[0]] == 1)).mean(),
                            both=((w[x[0]] == 1) & (w[y[0]] == 1)).mean(), neither=((w[x[0]] == 0) & (w[y[0]] == 0)).mean()))
    TW = pd.DataFrame(win)
    TW.to_csv(os.path.join(TAB, "expD_winner.csv"), index=False)
    # background (non-conflict) rules: does adding a conflict hurt the other rules? compare XY vs mean(X,Y)
    bg = D[D.conflict_role.isna()]
    TBG = bg.groupby(["model", "pair", "c"]).followed.mean().unstack(2)
    TBG.to_csv(os.path.join(TAB, "expD_background.csv"))
    # word counts in the soft length pair
    meta = pd.read_parquet(os.path.join(ROOT, "results", "generations_meta.parquet"))
    wc = meta[meta.cond.str.startswith("length")].groupby(["model", "cond"]).words.median().unstack(1)
    wc["N0_baseline"] = meta[meta.cond == "N0"].groupby("model").words.median()
    wc.to_csv(os.path.join(TAB, "expD_wordcounts.csv"))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ Exp E: count at ~4k tokens vs Exp A
    E = df[df.exp == "E"]
    rowsE = []
    for m in models:
        for n in [10, 20, 40]:
            a = A[(A.model == m) & (A.n_rules == n)].followed.mean()
            e = E[(E.model == m) & (E.n_rules == n)].followed.mean() if not E.empty else np.nan
            rowsE.append(dict(model=m, n_rules=n, list_short=a, interleaved_4k=e))
        b5 = B[(B.model == m) & (B.filler == 4000)].followed.mean()
        rowsE.append(dict(model=m, n_rules=5, list_short=A[(A.model == m) & (A.n_rules == 5)].followed.mean(),
                          interleaved_4k=b5))
    TE = pd.DataFrame(rowsE).sort_values(["model", "n_rules"])
    TE.to_csv(os.path.join(TAB, "expE_count_at_4k.csv"), index=False)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ per-rule difficulty (Exp A, N=1 vs 40)
    pr = A[A.n_rules > 0].groupby(["rule", "n_rules"]).followed.mean().unstack(1)
    pr["base"] = base.loc[pr.index].mean(axis=1)
    pr.sort_values(1).to_csv(os.path.join(TAB, "per_rule_expA.csv"))

    json.dump(out, open(os.path.join(ROOT, "results", "stats.json"), "w"), indent=1, default=float)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ figures
    cmap = plt.get_cmap("viridis")
    col = {m: cmap(i / max(1, len(models) - 1)) for i, m in enumerate(models)}
    ls = {"Qwen2.5": "-", "Llama-3": "--", "Qwen3": ":"}

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 4.5))
    for m in models:
        t = TA[(TA.model == m) & (TA.n_rules > 0)]
        ax[0].plot(t.n_rules, t.compliance, ls[MODELS[m][1]], marker="o", color=col[m], label=m)
        ax[0].fill_between(t.n_rules, t.lo, t.hi, color=col[m], alpha=0.12)
        ax[1].plot(t.n_rules, t.all_followed, ls[MODELS[m][1]], marker="o", color=col[m], label=m)
    ax[0].set(xlabel="number of rules in system prompt (N)", ylabel="per-rule compliance",
              title="Exp A: per-rule compliance vs rule count", xscale="log")
    ax[1].set(xlabel="number of rules (N)", ylabel="fraction of responses following ALL rules",
              title="Exp A: all-rules-followed rate", xscale="log")
    for a in ax:
        a.set_xticks([1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 40]); a.set_xticklabels([1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 40]); a.grid(alpha=0.3)
    ax[0].legend(fontsize=8, ncol=2)
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(os.path.join(FIG, "expA_count.png"), dpi=150); plt.close(fig)

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4.5))
    for m in models:
        t = TB[TB.model == m]
        ax.plot(t.sys_tokens, t.compliance, ls[MODELS[m][1]], marker="o", color=col[m], label=m)
        ax.fill_between(t.sys_tokens, t.lo, t.hi, color=col[m], alpha=0.12)
    ax.set(xscale="log", xlabel="system prompt length (tokens, log scale)", ylabel="per-rule compliance (5 rules)",
           title="Exp B: compliance vs system prompt length (rule count fixed at 5)")
    ax.axvline(500, color="gray", lw=0.8, ls=":")
    ax.grid(alpha=0.3); ax.legend(fontsize=8, ncol=2)
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(os.path.join(FIG, "expB_length.png"), dpi=150); plt.close(fig)

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 4.5))
    for s in dec.columns:
        ax[0].plot((dec.index + 0.5) / 10, dec[s], marker="o", label=s)
    ax[0].set(xlabel="relative position of rule in system prompt", ylabel="compliance (all models pooled)",
              title="Position effect by prompt structure"); ax[0].legend(fontsize=8); ax[0].grid(alpha=0.3)
    for m in models:
        ax[1].plot((decm.index + 0.5) / 10, decm[m], ls[MODELS[m][1]], marker=".", color=col[m], label=m)
    ax[1].set(xlabel="relative position", ylabel="compliance (pooled over A/B/E)", title="Position effect by model")
    ax[1].legend(fontsize=7, ncol=2); ax[1].grid(alpha=0.3)
    for a in ax:
        a.axvspan(0, 0.2, color="gray", alpha=0.08); a.axvspan(0.8, 1.0, color="gray", alpha=0.08)
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(os.path.join(FIG, "position.png"), dpi=150); plt.close(fig)

    fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, len(CONFLICTS), figsize=(16, 4.2), sharey=True)
    for a, (pair, (x, y)) in zip(axs, CONFLICTS.items()):
        t = TD[(TD.pair == pair) & (TD.model != "ALL")]
        xs = np.arange(len(models))
        for k, (role, c) in enumerate([("X", "tab:blue"), ("Y", "tab:orange")]):
            tt = t[t.role == role].set_index("model").loc[models]
            a.bar(xs + (k - 0.5) * 0.4, tt.alone, 0.4, color=c, alpha=0.35, label=f"{tt.rule.iloc[0]} alone")
            a.bar(xs + (k - 0.5) * 0.4, tt.both, 0.4, color=c, fill=False, edgecolor=c, hatch="//",
                  label=f"{tt.rule.iloc[0]} + conflict")
        a.set_xticks(xs); a.set_xticklabels(models, rotation=70, fontsize=7); a.set_title(pair)
        a.legend(fontsize=6)
    axs[0].set_ylabel("compliance")
    fig.suptitle("Exp D: compliance on each rule of a conflicting pair, alone (solid) vs with its contradiction (hatched)")
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(os.path.join(FIG, "expD_conflict.png"), dpi=150); plt.close(fig)

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4.5))
    for m in models:
        t = TE[TE.model == m]
        ax.plot(t.n_rules, t.list_short, ls[MODELS[m][1]], marker="o", color=col[m], label=f"{m}")
        ax.plot(t.n_rules, t.interleaved_4k, ls[MODELS[m][1]], marker="x", color=col[m], alpha=0.6)
    ax.set(xscale="log", xlabel="number of rules", ylabel="per-rule compliance",
           title="Rule count: short list (o) vs interleaved in ~4k-token prompt (x)")
    ax.set_xticks([5, 10, 20, 40]); ax.set_xticklabels([5, 10, 20, 40]); ax.grid(alpha=0.3); ax.legend(fontsize=7, ncol=2)
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(os.path.join(FIG, "expE_count_long.png"), dpi=150); plt.close(fig)

    pd.set_option("display.width", 250)
    print("== Exp A\n", TA.pivot(index="n_rules", columns="model", values="compliance").round(3)[models].to_string())
    print("== saturation\n", TS.round(3).to_string())
    print("== Exp B\n", TB.pivot(index="filler", columns="model", values="compliance").round(3)[models].to_string())
    print("== Exp B slopes\n", TBs.round(3).to_string())
    print("== pooled B", out["expB_pooled_ge500"])
    print("== position\n", TP[TP.source == "ALL"].round(3).to_string())
    print("== position by source (ALL models)\n", TP[TP.model == "ALL"].round(3).to_string())
    print("== Exp D\n", TD[TD.model == "ALL"].round(3).to_string())
    print("== Exp D per model rel change\n", TD[TD.model != "ALL"].pivot_table(index="model", columns=["pair", "role"], values="rel_change").round(2).to_string())
    print("== winners\n", TW.round(2).to_string())
    print("== background\n", TBG.round(3).to_string())

toolu_01GjKrSkQVSgz4dQrFC8w2Lj.content:
"""Statistical analysis + figures for all hypotheses. Reads results/rule_scores.parquet (from score.py).

Outputs: results/tables/*.csv, results/stats.json, figures/*.png
Uncertainty: item-clustered bootstrap (resample the 100 user queries; 2000 resamples, seed 0) unless noted.
"""
import json
import os
import warnings

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests
from scipy import stats

from rules import BANK, CONFLICTS

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
TAB = os.path.join(ROOT, "results", "tables")
FIG = os.path.join(ROOT, "figures")
os.makedirs(TAB, exist_ok=True)
os.makedirs(FIG, exist_ok=True)
B_RESAMPLES = 2000
RNG = np.random.default_rng(0)

# Model metadata: display order, parameter count (B), family
MODELS = {
    "qwen2.5-0.5b": (0.5, "Qwen2.5"), "llama3.2-1b": (1.2, "Llama-3"), "qwen2.5-1.5b": (1.5, "Qwen2.5"),
    "qwen2.5-3b": (3.1, "Qwen2.5"), "llama3.2-3b": (3.2, "Llama-3"), "qwen2.5-7b": (7.6, "Qwen2.5"),
    "llama3.1-8b": (8.0, "Llama-3"), "qwen3-8b": (8.2, "Qwen3"), "qwen2.5-14b": (14.7, "Qwen2.5"),
}
BANK_IDS = [r[0] for r in BANK]


def size_class(m):
    p = MODELS[m][0]
    return "<3B" if p < 3 else ("3B" if p < 7 else ">=7B")


def boot_items(df, stat, n=B_RESAMPLES):
    """Item-clustered bootstrap of stat(df) -> (point, lo, hi). stat takes a dataframe."""
    items = df["item"].unique()
    groups = {i: g for i, g in df.groupby("item")}
    point = stat(df)
    vals = []
    for _ in range(n):
        samp = RNG.choice(items, len(items), replace=True)
        d = pd.concat([groups[i] for i in samp], ignore_index=True)
        vals.append(stat(d))
    vals = np.array(vals)
    return point, np.nanpercentile(vals, 2.5), np.nanpercentile(vals, 97.5), vals


def item_boot_means(per_item, n=B_RESAMPLES):
    """Fast bootstrap for statistics that are means over items: per_item is an (items x k) array of per-item
    means; returns bootstrap distribution of column means (n x k)."""
    idx = RNG.integers(0, per_item.shape[0], size=(n, per_item.shape[0]))
    return np.nanmean(per_item[idx], axis=1)


def main():
    df = pd.read_parquet(os.path.join(ROOT, "results", "rule_scores.parquet"))
    df = df[df.model.isin(MODELS)]
    models = [m for m in MODELS if m in df.model.unique()]
    base = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(ROOT, "results", "base_rates.csv"), index_col=0)
    df["base"] = [base.at[r, m] if (r in base.index and m in base.columns) else np.nan for r, m in zip(df.rule, df.model)]
    out = {"models": models}

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ Exp A: rule count
    A = df[df.exp == "A"]
    rowsA = []
    for m in models:
        d = A[A.model == m]
        for n, g in d.groupby("n_rules"):
            per_item = g.groupby("item").followed.mean()
            bm = item_boot_means(per_item.values[:, None])[:, 0]
            allf = g.groupby("item").followed.min()
            lift = (g.followed - g.base).groupby(g.item).mean()
            rowsA.append(dict(model=m, n_rules=n, compliance=per_item.mean(), lo=np.percentile(bm, 2.5),
                              hi=np.percentile(bm, 97.5), all_followed=allf.mean(), base=g.base.mean(),
                              lift=lift.mean(), sys_tokens=g.prompt_tokens.mean()))
    TA = pd.DataFrame(rowsA)
    TA.to_csv(os.path.join(TAB, "expA_count.csv"), index=False)

    # Saturation point: largest N whose compliance is within 5 pp of the model's N<=2 level, and a hinge fit.
    sat = []
    for m in models:
        t = TA[TA.model == m].set_index("n_rules")
        ref = t.loc[[1, 2], "compliance"].mean()
        d = A[(A.model == m)].copy()
        # hinge regression: compliance ~ a + b1*N + b2*max(0, N-k); pick k minimizing SSE (linear prob. model)
        best = None
        for k in [2, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30]:
            d["h"] = np.maximum(0, d.n_rules - k)
            f = smf.ols("followed ~ n_rules + h + C(rule)", data=d).fit()
            if best is None or f.ssr < best[1]:
                best = (k, f.ssr, f)
        k, _, f = best
        first_drop = next((n for n in [5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 40] if t.loc[n, "compliance"] < ref - 0.05), None)
        sat.append(dict(model=m, params_b=MODELS[m][0], size_class=size_class(m), ref_N1_2=ref,
                        comp_N10=t.loc[10, "compliance"], comp_N20=t.loc[20, "compliance"],
                        comp_N40=t.loc[40, "compliance"], first_N_5pp_below_ref=first_drop,
                        hinge_k=k, slope_before=f.params["n_rules"], slope_after=f.params["n_rules"] + f.params["h"]))
    TS = pd.DataFrame(sat)
    TS.to_csv(os.path.join(TAB, "expA_saturation.csv"), index=False)
    out["saturation"] = TS.to_dict("records")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ Exp B: length at fixed N=5
    B = df[df.exp == "B"]
    rowsB, slopes = [], []
    for m in models:
        d = B[B.model == m]
        for L, g in d.groupby("filler"):
            per_item = g.groupby("item").followed.mean()
            bm = item_boot_means(per_item.values[:, None])[:, 0]
            rowsB.append(dict(model=m, filler=L, sys_tokens=g.prompt_tokens.mean(), compliance=per_item.mean(),
                              lo=np.percentile(bm, 2.5), hi=np.percentile(bm, 97.5),
                              truncated=g.truncated.mean()))
        # per-doubling slope beyond ~500 tokens: OLS on log2(prompt tokens) with rule fixed effects,
        # item-cluster-robust SEs. Relative slope = slope / mean compliance at the ~500-token condition.
        for label, sub in [("all", d), ("ge500", d[d.filler >= 500])]:
            sub = sub.assign(l2=np.log2(sub.prompt_tokens))
            f = smf.ols("followed ~ l2 + C(rule)", data=sub).fit(cov_type="cluster", cov_kwds={"groups": sub.item})
            ref = d[d.filler == 500].followed.mean()
            lg = smf.logit("followed ~ l2 + C(rule)", data=sub).fit(disp=0, cov_type="cluster",
                                                                     cov_kwds={"groups": sub.item}) \
                if sub.followed.nunique() > 1 else None
            slopes.append(dict(model=m, range=label, slope_pp_per_doubling=100 * f.params["l2"],
                               ci_lo=100 * f.conf_int().loc["l2", 0], ci_hi=100 * f.conf_int().loc["l2", 1],
                               p=f.pvalues["l2"], rel_pct_per_doubling=100 * f.params["l2"] / ref,
                               logit_or_per_doubling=float(np.exp(lg.params["l2"])) if lg is not None else np.nan,
                               comp_500=ref, comp_8000=d[d.filler == 8000].followed.mean()))
    TB = pd.DataFrame(rowsB)
    TB.to_csv(os.path.join(TAB, "expB_length.csv"), index=False)
    TBs = pd.DataFrame(slopes)
    TBs["p_holm"] = np.nan
    msk = TBs.range == "ge500"
    TBs.loc[msk, "p_holm"] = multipletests(TBs.loc[msk, "p"], method="holm")[1]
    TBs.to_csv(os.path.join(TAB, "expB_slopes.csv"), index=False)
    # pooled across models (model x rule fixed effects)
    sub = B[B.filler >= 500].assign(l2=lambda x: np.log2(x.prompt_tokens))
    f = smf.ols("followed ~ l2 + C(rule):C(model) + C(model)", data=sub).fit(
        cov_type="cluster", cov_kwds={"groups": sub.item})
    out["expB_pooled_ge500"] = dict(slope_pp=100 * f.params["l2"], lo=100 * f.conf_int().loc["l2", 0],
                                    hi=100 * f.conf_int().loc["l2", 1], p=f.pvalues["l2"],
                                    rel_pct=100 * f.params["l2"] / B[B.filler == 500].followed.mean())

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ Position (A N>=10, B L>=1000, E)
    P = df[((df.exp == "A") & (df.n_rules >= 10)) | ((df.exp == "B") & (df.filler >= 1000)) | (df.exp == "E")].copy()
    P["bin"] = pd.cut(P.pos, [-0.01, 0.2, 0.8, 1.01], labels=["first20", "middle", "last20"])
    P["dec"] = np.minimum((P.pos * 10).astype(int), 9)
    P["src"] = P.exp.map({"A": "list (Exp A)", "B": "interleaved, N=5 (Exp B)", "E": "interleaved, 4k tok (Exp E)"})
    rowsP = []
    for m in models + ["ALL"]:
        for src in ["ALL"] + sorted(P.src.unique()):
            d = P if m == "ALL" else P[P.model == m]
            d = d if src == "ALL" else d[d.src == src]
            if d.empty:
                continue
            # per-item means by bin -> bootstrap ratio of edges to middle
            pi = d.pivot_table(index="item", columns="bin", values="followed", aggfunc="mean", observed=False)
            pi = pi[["first20", "middle", "last20"]].values
            bm = item_boot_means(pi)
            edge = lambda a: (a[..., 0] + a[..., 2]) / 2
            ratio_b = edge(bm) / bm[:, 1]
            pt = np.nanmean(pi, axis=0)
            # regression with rule (and condition) fixed effects, cluster by item
            f = smf.ols("followed ~ C(bin, Treatment('middle')) + C(rule) + C(cond)" +
                        (" + C(model)" if m == "ALL" else ""), data=d).fit(
                cov_type="cluster", cov_kwds={"groups": d.item})
            rowsP.append(dict(model=m, source=src, n=len(d), first20=pt[0], middle=pt[1], last20=pt[2],
                              edge_mid_ratio=edge(pt) / pt[1], ratio_lo=np.nanpercentile(ratio_b, 2.5),
                              ratio_hi=np.nanpercentile(ratio_b, 97.5),
                              fe_first_pp=100 * f.params["C(bin, Treatment('middle'))[T.first20]"],
                              fe_first_p=f.pvalues["C(bin, Treatment('middle'))[T.first20]"],
                              fe_last_pp=100 * f.params["C(bin, Treatment('middle'))[T.last20]"],
                              fe_last_p=f.pvalues["C(bin, Treatment('middle'))[T.last20]"]))
    TP = pd.DataFrame(rowsP)
    TP.to_csv(os.path.join(TAB, "position.csv"), index=False)
    dec = P.groupby(["src", "dec"]).followed.mean().unstack(0)
    dec.to_csv(os.path.join(TAB, "position_deciles.csv"))
    decm = P.groupby(["model", "dec"]).followed.mean().unstack(0)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ Exp D: conflicts
    D = df[df.exp == "D"].copy()
    D["c"] = D.cond.str.split(":").str[1]
    rowsD = []
    for m in models + ["ALL"]:
        for pair, (x, y) in CONFLICTS.items():
            for role, rid, alone in [("X", x[0], "X"), ("Y", y[0], "Y")]:
                d = D[(D.pair == pair) & (D.rule == rid)]
                d = d if m == "ALL" else d[d.model == m]
                a = d[d.c == alone].set_index(["model", "item"]).followed
                b = d[d.c == "XY"].set_index(["model", "item"]).followed
                j = pd.concat([a.rename("alone"), b.rename("both")], axis=1).dropna()
                n01 = int(((j.alone == 1) & (j.both == 0)).sum())
                n10 = int(((j.alone == 0) & (j.both == 1)).sum())
                p = stats.binomtest(n01, n01 + n10).pvalue if n01 + n10 else 1.0
                per_item = j.groupby(level="item").mean().values
                bm = item_boot_means(per_item)
                rel_b = (bm[:, 1] - bm[:, 0]) / bm[:, 0]
                rowsD.append(dict(model=m, pair=pair, role=role, rule=rid, alone=j.alone.mean(), both=j.both.mean(),
                                  diff_pp=100 * (j.both.mean() - j.alone.mean()),
                                  rel_change=(j.both.mean() - j.alone.mean()) / j.alone.mean() if j.alone.mean() else np.nan,
                                  rel_lo=np.nanpercentile(rel_b, 2.5), rel_hi=np.nanpercentile(rel_b, 97.5),
                                  mcnemar_p=p, n=len(j)))
    TD = pd.DataFrame(rowsD)
    msk = TD.model != "ALL"
    TD.loc[msk, "p_holm"] = multipletests(TD.loc[msk, "mcnemar_p"], method="holm")[1]
    TD.to_csv(os.path.join(TAB, "expD_conflict.csv"), index=False)
    # both members followed? and "who wins" in XY
    win = []
    for m in models:
        for pair, (x, y) in CONFLICTS.items():
            d = D[(D.model == m) & (D.pair == pair) & (D.c == "XY")]
            w = d.pivot_table(index="item", columns="rule", values="followed")
            win.append(dict(model=m, pair=pair, X_only=((w[x[0]] == 1) & (w[y[0]] == 0)).mean(),
                            Y_only=((w[x[0]] == 0) & (w[y[0]] == 1)).mean(),
                            both=((w[x[0]] == 1) & (w[y[0]] == 1)).mean(), neither=((w[x[0]] == 0) & (w[y[0]] == 0)).mean()))
    TW = pd.DataFrame(win)
    TW.to_csv(os.path.join(TAB, "expD_winner.csv"), index=False)
    # background (non-conflict) rules: does adding a conflict hurt the other rules? compare XY vs mean(X,Y)
    bg = D[D.conflict_role.isna()]
    TBG = bg.groupby(["model", "pair", "c"]).followed.mean().unstack(2)
    TBG.to_csv(os.path.join(TAB, "expD_background.csv"))
    # word counts in the soft length pair
    meta = pd.read_parquet(os.path.join(ROOT, "results", "generations_meta.parquet"))
    wc = meta[meta.cond.str.startswith("length")].groupby(["model", "cond"]).words.median().unstack(1)
    wc["N0_baseline"] = meta[meta.cond == "N0"].groupby("model").words.median()
    wc.to_csv(os.path.join(TAB, "expD_wordcounts.csv"))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ Exp E: count at ~4k tokens vs Exp A
    E = df[df.exp == "E"]
    rowsE = []
    for m in models:
        for n in [10, 20, 40]:
            a = A[(A.model == m) & (A.n_rules == n)].followed.mean()
            e = E[(E.model == m) & (E.n_rules == n)].followed.mean() if not E.empty else np.nan
            rowsE.append(dict(model=m, n_rules=n, list_short=a, interleaved_4k=e))
        b5 = B[(B.model == m) & (B.filler == 4000)].followed.mean()
        rowsE.append(dict(model=m, n_rules=5, list_short=A[(A.model == m) & (A.n_rules == 5)].followed.mean(),
                          interleaved_4k=b5))
    TE = pd.DataFrame(rowsE).sort_values(["model", "n_rules"])
    TE.to_csv(os.path.join(TAB, "expE_count_at_4k.csv"), index=False)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ per-rule difficulty (Exp A, N=1 vs 40)
    pr = A[A.n_rules > 0].groupby(["rule", "n_rules"]).followed.mean().unstack(1)
    pr["base"] = base.loc[pr.index].mean(axis=1)
    pr.sort_values(1).to_csv(os.path.join(TAB, "per_rule_expA.csv"))

    json.dump(out, open(os.path.join(ROOT, "results", "stats.json"), "w"), indent=1, default=float)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ figures
    cmap = plt.get_cmap("viridis")
    col = {m: cmap(i / max(1, len(models) - 1)) for i, m in enumerate(models)}
    ls = {"Qwen2.5": "-", "Llama-3": "--", "Qwen3": ":"}

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 4.5))
    for m in models:
        t = TA[(TA.model == m) & (TA.n_rules > 0)]
        ax[0].plot(t.n_rules, t.compliance, ls[MODELS[m][1]], marker="o", color=col[m], label=m)
        ax[0].fill_between(t.n_rules, t.lo, t.hi, color=col[m], alpha=0.12)
        ax[1].plot(t.n_rules, t.all_followed, ls[MODELS[m][1]], marker="o", color=col[m], label=m)
    ax[0].set(xlabel="number of rules in system prompt (N)", ylabel="per-rule compliance",
              title="Exp A: per-rule compliance vs rule count", xscale="log")
    ax[1].set(xlabel="number of rules (N)", ylabel="fraction of responses following ALL rules",
              title="Exp A: all-rules-followed rate", xscale="log")
    for a in ax:
        a.set_xticks([1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 40]); a.set_xticklabels([1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 40]); a.grid(alpha=0.3)
    ax[0].legend(fontsize=8, ncol=2)
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(os.path.join(FIG, "expA_count.png"), dpi=150); plt.close(fig)

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4.5))
    for m in models:
        t = TB[TB.model == m]
        ax.plot(t.sys_tokens, t.compliance, ls[MODELS[m][1]], marker="o", color=col[m], label=m)
        ax.fill_between(t.sys_tokens, t.lo, t.hi, color=col[m], alpha=0.12)
    ax.set(xscale="log", xlabel="system prompt length (tokens, log scale)", ylabel="per-rule compliance (5 rules)",
           title="Exp B: compliance vs system prompt length (rule count fixed at 5)")
    ax.axvline(500, color="gray", lw=0.8, ls=":")
    ax.grid(alpha=0.3); ax.legend(fontsize=8, ncol=2)
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(os.path.join(FIG, "expB_length.png"), dpi=150); plt.close(fig)

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 4.5))
    for s in dec.columns:
        ax[0].plot((dec.index + 0.5) / 10, dec[s], marker="o", label=s)
    ax[0].set(xlabel="relative position of rule in system prompt", ylabel="compliance (all models pooled)",
              title="Position effect by prompt structure"); ax[0].legend(fontsize=8); ax[0].grid(alpha=0.3)
    for m in models:
        ax[1].plot((decm.index + 0.5) / 10, decm[m], ls[MODELS[m][1]], marker=".", color=col[m], label=m)
    ax[1].set(xlabel="relative position", ylabel="compliance (pooled over A/B/E)", title="Position effect by model")
    ax[1].legend(fontsize=7, ncol=2); ax[1].grid(alpha=0.3)
    for a in ax:
        a.axvspan(0, 0.2, color="gray", alpha=0.08); a.axvspan(0.8, 1.0, color="gray", alpha=0.08)
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(os.path.join(FIG, "position.png"), dpi=150); plt.close(fig)

    fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, len(CONFLICTS), figsize=(16, 4.2), sharey=True)
    for a, (pair, (x, y)) in zip(axs, CONFLICTS.items()):
        t = TD[(TD.pair == pair) & (TD.model != "ALL")]
        xs = np.arange(len(models))
        for k, (role, c) in enumerate([("X", "tab:blue"), ("Y", "tab:orange")]):
            tt = t[t.role == role].set_index("model").loc[models]
            a.bar(xs + (k - 0.5) * 0.4, tt.alone, 0.4, color=c, alpha=0.35, label=f"{tt.rule.iloc[0]} alone")
            a.bar(xs + (k - 0.5) * 0.4, tt.both, 0.4, color=c, fill=False, edgecolor=c, hatch="//",
                  label=f"{tt.rule.iloc[0]} + conflict")
        a.set_xticks(xs); a.set_xticklabels(models, rotation=70, fontsize=7); a.set_title(pair)
        a.legend(fontsize=6)
    axs[0].set_ylabel("compliance")
    fig.suptitle("Exp D: compliance on each rule of a conflicting pair, alone (solid) vs with its contradiction (hatched)")
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(os.path.join(FIG, "expD_conflict.png"), dpi=150); plt.close(fig)

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4.5))
    for m in models:
        t = TE[TE.model == m]
        ax.plot(t.n_rules, t.list_short, ls[MODELS[m][1]], marker="o", color=col[m], label=f"{m}")
        ax.plot(t.n_rules, t.interleaved_4k, ls[MODELS[m][1]], marker="x", color=col[m], alpha=0.6)
    ax.set(xscale="log", xlabel="number of rules", ylabel="per-rule compliance",
           title="Rule count: short list (o) vs interleaved in ~4k-token prompt (x)")
    ax.set_xticks([5, 10, 20, 40]); ax.set_xticklabels([5, 10, 20, 40]); ax.grid(alpha=0.3); ax.legend(fontsize=7, ncol=2)
    fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(os.path.join(FIG, "expE_count_long.png"), dpi=150); plt.close(fig)

    pd.set_option("display.width", 250)
    print("== Exp A\n", TA.pivot(index="n_rules", columns="model", values="compliance").round(3)[models].to_string())
    print("== saturation\n", TS.round(3).to_string())
    print("== Exp B\n", TB.pivot(index="filler", columns="model", values="compliance").round(3)[models].to_string())
    print("== Exp B slopes\n", TBs.round(3).to_string())
    print("== pooled B", out["expB_pooled_ge500"])
    print("== position\n", TP[TP.source == "ALL"].round(3).to_string())
    print("== position by source (ALL models)\n", TP[TP.model == "ALL"].round(3).to_string())
    print("== Exp D\n", TD[TD.model == "ALL"].round(3).to_string())
    print("== Exp D per model rel change\n", TD[TD.model != "ALL"].pivot_table(index="model", columns=["pair", "role"], values="rel_change").round(2).to_string())
    print("== winners\n", TW.round(2).to_string())
    print("== background\n", TBG.round(3).to_string())
    print("== wordcounts\n", wc.to_string())
    print("== Exp E\n", TE.round(3).to_string())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
